● Ops runbook

Login, deploy, bind a domain

Every command for standing up FHIRBridge on Azure Container Apps and putting a real domain with a free managed certificate in front of it — from az login to a green padlock.

Resource group rg-tusharpuri Storage account fhirbridgedeploy Blob container deploy Example prefix segue14

Live Deploy-to-Azure links generated 2026-08-29

Freshly published by publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1 — open either one directly to click through the wizard (and take screenshots). Re-run phase 02 any time to mint new ones; old links still work until the underlying files change.

Step 1 (full stack) — open in Portal ↗

Step 2 (domain + SSL) — open in Portal ↗

! Two things to know before you start:

1. DNS needs time to propagate after Step 1 and after you create the CNAME/TXT records — Step 2 will fail with InvalidCustomHostNameValidation if you deploy it before that propagation finishes (minutes to hours depending on your DNS provider); just wait and redeploy.

2. Even after Step 1 says "complete," give it 10–15 minutes before trying to log in — Redis takes a little while to finish starting up after the container apps come online, and login will not work until it's ready. A deployment that finished successfully does not mean the app is ready to use yet. 
flowchart LR
    A["az login"] --> B["publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1"]
    B --> C["Step 1\nmain.bicep"]
    C --> D["Read FQDN +\nverification ID"]
    D --> E["Create CNAME + TXT\nat DNS provider"]
    E --> F{"DNS resolves?"}
    F -- "not yet" --> E
    F -- "yes" --> G["Step 2\ncustom-domain.bicep\n(one deploy)"]
    G --> H["https://yourdomain\nis live"]
01

Login & prerequisites

Confirm the Azure CLI is signed in to the right tenant and subscription before touching anything else — every command below assumes this is already done.

Azure CLI
# Sign in (opens a browser window)
az login

# Confirm you're on the right subscription
az account show --query name -o tsv

# Switch subscription if needed
az account set --subscription "<subscription name or ID>"

# Confirm the target resource group exists (create it if this is a fresh environment)
az group show --name rg-tusharpuri
az group create --name rg-tusharpuri --location <region>   # only if it doesn't exist yet
02

Publish deploy artifacts

Compiles the Bicep templates to ARM JSON and uploads both Deploy-to-Azure packages (Step 1 and Step 2) to blob storage. Run this once, and again any time main.bicep, custom-domain.bicep, or either createUiDefinition*.json changes — it re-publishes and hands you fresh, cache-busted Portal links.

PowerShell
cd containerization/azure-deploy
.\publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1 -StorageAccount fhirbridgedeploy -ResourceGroup rg-tusharpuri
→ Prints two links — Step 1 (full-stack deploy) and Step 2 (domain/certificate binder) — and opens Step 1 in your browser automatically. This is how you get the deploy URLs: they are generated fresh by this script, not fixed addresses, since each publish appends a new ?v=<timestamp> to bust the Portal's blob cache.
! Needs write access to the storage account (Storage Blob Data Contributor, or Contributor for key-based fallback). The script tries --auth-mode login first and falls back to --auth-mode key automatically.
03

Step 1 — deploy the stack

Creates the environment, all 7 container apps (FHIRBridge app, Demo app, Worker, SQL Server, Redis, Terminology server + its own Postgres), Log Analytics, and the storage account behind them — everything in main.bicep. No domain field actually activates anything here — a container app's verification ID only exists once the app itself does, so asking for a domain on this first deploy always fails; the 3 domain boxes on this wizard are reminders only (phase 06 does the real activation).

Via the Portal (recommended)

Open the Step 1 link at the top of this page (or reprint it with publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1). Work through 6 tabs — Basics, FHIRBridge Settings, Container Sizes, Version, Network Access, What Gets Created — then Review + create. Full field-by-field detail for every tab is below.

Tab 1 — Basics

FieldTypeWhere the value comes from
SubscriptionAzure's built-in pickerWhichever subscription you want billed — same one az account show reports if you're using the CLI path instead
Resource groupAzure's built-in pickerPick an existing one, or create new inline. This runbook's examples use rg-tusharpuri
RegionAzure's built-in region dropdownAny region where Microsoft.App, Microsoft.OperationalInsights, and Microsoft.Storage are available — i.e. any standard Azure region. Every resource in the deployment lands here
namePrefixText boxYour own choice — builds every resource name (<prefix>-app, <prefix>-sqlserver, etc.). Lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, starts with a letter, 2–21 characters. Default: fhirbridge

Tab 2 — FHIRBridge Settings (5 fields, 4 are password + confirm pairs)

Field labelConfirm field labelParameterWhere the value comes from
SQL Server SA password Confirm password sqlSaPassword You choose it. Must be 8+ characters with upper case, lower case, and a digit (SQL Server's own complexity policy) — this becomes the SA login for the SQL Server Express container
API signing key Confirm signing key jwtSigningKey You generate it — it's not a login password, it's FHIRBridge.Api's HS256 JWT signing key (Authentication:SigningKey). Any random string, 32+ characters — e.g. openssl rand -base64 32 or a password manager's generator
Redis password Confirm password redisPassword You choose it. 8+ characters — passed to Redis as --requirepass, defense-in-depth on top of network isolation
Terminology server database password Confirm password hapiTerminologyPostgresPassword You choose it. 8+ characters — the Postgres role backing the HAPI terminology server's own internal schema (not the app's SQL Server database)
! A 5th field on this same tab — Redis TLS certificate thumbprint (redisTrustedCertificateThumbprint) — looks similar but is a plain text box with no confirm field, and you don't choose its value: run containerization/docker/redis-tls/generate-cert.ps1 (or .sh) once, before building images, and it prints a 40-character SHA-1 thumbprint (e.g. 8638036B0BE54FADF44EEDBFCD2CEC1A80BBB37F) — paste that exact value here. FHIRBridge refuses the Redis connection outright if it doesn't match what Redis actually presents.

Tab 3 — Container Sizes (7 identical dropdowns)

Every dropdown offers the exact same 4 options — Azure Container Apps' Consumption plan only accepts CPU/memory at fixed pairs, so the wizard picks from a preset ladder instead of raw numbers:

OptionCPU / memory
Small0.25 CPU / 0.5 GB
Medium0.5 CPU / 1 GB
Large1.0 CPU / 2 GB
XLarge2.0 CPU / 4 GB
DropdownParameterDefaultNotes
SQL Server sizesqlServerSizeLargeBump to XLarge if first-run initialization OOM-kills on Large — SQL Server's one-time setup can spike harder than steady state
Redis sizeredisSizeMediumIts own cache/queue memory need, separate from what it persists to its file share
FHIRBridge app sizefhirbridgeAppSizeMediumRuns both FHIRBridge.Api and FHIRBridge.Gateway in this one container
Demo app sizedemoAppSizeSmallThe lightweight demo application
Worker sizeworkerSizeSmallBackground scheduler/pipeline processor — no HTTP endpoint
Terminology server sizehapiTerminologySizeLargeJava/Spring — benefits from memory headroom beyond what the CPU size alone suggests
Terminology server database sizehapiTerminologyPostgresSizeMediumThe Postgres database backing the terminology server's own schema

Tab 4 — Version

FieldTypeWhere the value comes from
Version to installimageTagThe vendor's release list on the image registry (seguebuilds.azurecr.io) — ask whoever manages releases which tags are available. Default: v1.0.0
i The registry itself (imageRegistryServer/imageRegistryUsername/imageRegistryPassword) is not a field you see in the Portal wizard at all — it's silently supplied by the wizard's own output mapping (pointed at the vendor's registry), so a one-click customer never has to know or enter it. It's only something you supply yourself on the CLI path below.

Tab 5 — Network Access

FieldTypeWhere the value comes from
FHIRBridge app domain (optional, informational only)fhirbridgeAppIntendedDomainYour own planned future domain, e.g. app.customer.com. Not activated by this deploy — just echoed back in the outputs as a reminder for phase 06
Demo app domain (optional, informational only)demoAppIntendedDomainSame — planned future domain, reminder only
Terminology server domain (optional, informational only)hapiTerminologyIntendedDomainSame — planned future domain, reminder only
Expose the terminology server externallyhapiTerminologyExternalAccessCheckbox, default off. Leave unchecked unless something outside this environment (a separate admin tool, a third-party integration) needs to reach it directly — the FHIRBridge app/Worker always reach it internally either way. Not needed just to give it a domain later — phase 06 turns this on automatically when you set a domain for it

Tab 6 — What Gets Created (review, no input)

Pure summary — 7 container apps, 1 Container Apps environment, 1 Log Analytics workspace, 1 storage account with 4 Azure File shares (SQL data, Redis data, terminology server data, DataProtection keys). Confirms domains are optional and activated separately (phase 06), and that SQL Server/Redis/Terminology server stay internal-only by default. Double-check the previous 5 tabs, then continue to Review + create.

Azure CLI — alternative (every real main.bicep parameter)
az deployment group create \
  --resource-group rg-tusharpuri \
  --template-file main.bicep \
  --parameters \
    namePrefix=segue14 \
    sqlSaPassword='<strong-password>' \
    jwtSigningKey='<random-32-plus-char-key>' \
    redisPassword='<strong-password>' \
    redisTrustedCertificateThumbprint='<40-char-SHA1-from-generate-cert.ps1>' \
    hapiTerminologyPostgresPassword='<strong-password>' \
    imageRegistryServer='<your-registry>.azurecr.io' \
    imageRegistryUsername='<registry-username>' \
    imageRegistryPassword='<registry-password>' \
    imageTag='v1.0.0' \
    sqlServerSize=Large redisSize=Medium fhirbridgeAppSize=Medium \
    demoAppSize=Small workerSize=Small hapiTerminologySize=Large \
    hapiTerminologyPostgresSize=Medium \
    hapiTerminologyExternalAccess=false

The Portal wizard never asks for imageRegistryServer/Username/Password (baked in automatically — see the callout above) — the CLI path does, since there's no wizard supplying it for you. location, sqlPort, redisPort, the 3 *CustomDomain params, and bindCustomDomainCertificates all have safe defaults and are intentionally left off here — see main.bicep's own parameter declarations if you need to override one.

Tab 7 — Review + create

Deployment in progress

Resources appear incrementally as Azure creates them — storage and Log Analytics first (no dependencies), then the environment, then all 7 container apps and their file shares once the environment exists.

04

Get the app URLs & verification ID

The default FQDN and the domain-verification ID (the value the TXT record needs) exist the moment each app does — no Step 2 deploy required to learn them. Four ways to get them, in order of convenience:

A — Step 1's own outputs
az deployment group show \
  --resource-group rg-tusharpuri \
  --name main \
  --query properties.outputs
B — az containerapp show
az containerapp show \
  --name segue14-app \
  --resource-group rg-tusharpuri \
  --query "{fqdn:properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn, verificationId:properties.customDomainVerificationId}" \
  -o json
C — discovery script
.\containerization\scripts\discover-custom-domains.ps1
# or: ./containerization/scripts/discover-custom-domains.sh
# Prompts for resource group + name prefix, lists all 3 apps' FQDN + verification ID,
# and computes the exact CNAME/TXT values once you type a domain.
D Or just open the Step 2 wizard itself — each of its 3 tabs shows the live default URL and verification ID before you've even typed a domain.
05

Create DNS records

At your DNS provider, per app you want a domain on:

TypeNameValue
CNAMEyour.domain<the app's FQDN from step 04>
TXTasuid.your.domain<the verification ID from step 04>
Check propagation
# Windows
Resolve-DnsName your.domain -Type CNAME
Resolve-DnsName asuid.your.domain -Type TXT

# macOS / Linux
dig +short CNAME your.domain
dig +short TXT asuid.your.domain
! DNS must resolve before Step 2, not just before the certificate — Azure validates the TXT record the moment the hostname is registered. Propagation takes minutes to hours depending on your provider.

All 6 records (3 CNAME + 3 TXT), as they ended up saved at the DNS provider for this run:

06

Step 2 — bind domain + SSL

One deployment registers the hostname, creates the free Azure-managed certificate, and binds it — sequenced internally so Azure never sees them out of order. All 3 domain fields (FHIRBridge app, Demo app, Terminology server) are independent and optional.

Via the Portal (recommended)

Open the Step 2 URL from publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1. Enter the same namePrefix as Step 1, fill in whichever domain field(s) you want, deploy.

Tab 1 — FHIRBridge app

Creating the matching records at the DNS provider (GoDaddy, in this run):

Tab 2 — Demo app

Creating the matching records at the DNS provider:

Tab 3 — Terminology server

Creating the matching records at the DNS provider:

Each of the 3 tabs is laid out identically: app name → live default URL + domain-verification ID (fetched live from Azure the moment the tab opens) → an optional domain text box → the exact CNAME/TXT records to create, once you type a domain. See phase 04 for exactly how those live values are pulled.

Azure CLI — alternative
az deployment group create \
  --resource-group rg-tusharpuri \
  --template-file custom-domain.bicep \
  --parameters namePrefix=segue14 \
               fhirbridgeAppDomain=segueapp.pegasusone.com \
               demoAppDomain=seguedemo.pegasusone.com \
               hapiTerminologyDomain=segueterm.pegasusone.com
               # leave any of the 3 domain params off to skip that app entirely this run
✓ Safe to re-run any time — a domain that's already bound is a no-op; the certificate is reused, not recreated, and the app stays reachable throughout.
✕ If DNS wasn't actually ready, this fails cleanly with InvalidCustomHostNameValidation. Wait for propagation, then re-run the exact same command.

Review + create

What the internal register→bind sequencing looks like live

This is the proof, captured mid-deploy, that custom-domain.bicep's two module calls really do run in order — every register-*-customdomain module finishes before any bind-*-customdomain module starts, for all 3 apps:

07

Automate it

Folds phases 04–06 into one command: reads each app's FQDN + verification ID, prints the DNS records to create, polls DNS itself until they resolve, then deploys custom-domain.bicep exactly once and prints the final live URLs. Anything already certificate-bound is reported and skipped.

PowerShell
.\containerization\scripts\auto-bind-custom-domain.ps1 `
  -ResourceGroup rg-tusharpuri `
  -NamePrefix segue14 `
  -FhirbridgeAppDomain segueapp.pegasusone.com `
  -DemoAppDomain seguedemo.pegasusone.com `
  -HapiTerminologyDomain segueterm.pegasusone.com
  # optional: -WaitTimeoutMinutes 30 -WaitPollSeconds 30 (both default to 30)
Bash
./auto-bind-custom-domain.sh \
  -g rg-tusharpuri -p segue14 \
  -a segueapp.pegasusone.com \
  -d seguedemo.pegasusone.com \
  -t segueterm.pegasusone.com
  # optional: -w 30 (timeout minutes) -s 30 (poll interval seconds)
08

Verify live

Bash / PowerShell
curl -I https://segueapp.pegasusone.com
# expect: HTTP/2 200, and a valid certificate (check the padlock in a browser)
09

First login — create the SuperAdmin

The FHIRBridge app and Demo app are both live at this point, but the FHIRBridge app has no user account yet. Opening it for the first time redirects to a one-time setup wizard that creates the initial SuperAdmin account and configures the outbound email server.

FHIRBridge app — one-time setup

i Click Create SuperAdmin & Continue and you're signed in automatically as that account — no separate login step.

Demo app and Terminology server — no setup needed

The other two public apps are ready immediately, no first-run wizard:

Mandatory 2FA setup (forced on first login)

! Give it 10–15 minutes after Step 1 finishes before attempting any of this. Redis is still starting up for a short while after the container apps report "Running" — login attempts (including this first-run SuperAdmin flow) fail until it's ready, even though the deployment itself already says complete.

Bicep templates

Both steps compile from Bicep to ARM JSON before anything is uploaded. What follows: where the source lives, how to get the URL to any compiled artifact directly (not just the Portal wizard link from phase 02), and the exact loop for editing one safely.

FilePurpose
main.bicepStep 1 — environment, all container apps, SQL, Redis, storage, secrets
custom-domain.bicepStep 2 — domain + certificate binding for the 3 public-facing apps
custom-domain-app-update.bicepModule used internally by custom-domain.bicep to avoid a circular dependency — never deployed directly
createUiDefinition.jsonStep 1 Portal wizard definition (hand-written JSON, nothing to compile)
createUiDefinition.custom-domain.jsonStep 2 Portal wizard definition (same — hand-written, not compiled)

Get the URL for any step

Easiest option: publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1 (phase 02) already prints ready-to-use Portal deep-links for both steps in one go — that's all you need most of the time.

To grab the raw blob URL for one specific compiled file instead (e.g. to hand someone the template URL directly, or build a "Deploy to Azure" badge):

Azure CLI
# Step 1
az storage blob url --account-name fhirbridgedeploy --container-name deploy --name main.json -o tsv
az storage blob url --account-name fhirbridgedeploy --container-name deploy --name createUiDefinition.json -o tsv

# Step 2
az storage blob url --account-name fhirbridgedeploy --container-name deploy --name custom-domain.json -o tsv
az storage blob url --account-name fhirbridgedeploy --container-name deploy --name createUiDefinition.custom-domain.json -o tsv
! These bare URLs never change name, but the Portal caches blobs aggressively. The ?v=<timestamp> query param publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1 appends is what actually forces a fresh fetch — a bare URL you grab yourself can silently serve a stale cached copy.

Compose a full Deploy-to-Azure link yourself from any template URL + wizard URL pair:

Pattern
https://portal.azure.com/#create/Microsoft.Template/uri/<url-encoded template.json URL>/createUIDefinitionUri/<url-encoded createUiDefinition.json URL>
# Step 1: main.json + createUiDefinition.json
# Step 2: custom-domain.json + createUiDefinition.custom-domain.json

Update a Bicep template

1 — edit, then recompile
cd containerization/azure-deploy
# edit main.bicep / custom-domain.bicep / custom-domain-app-update.bicep, then:
az bicep build --file main.bicep --outfile main.json
az bicep build --file custom-domain.bicep --outfile custom-domain.json
✕ publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1 only compiles a .bicep file if its .json output doesn't already exist. If you've built before, editing the .bicep source and re-running the publish script alone will silently re-upload the stale JSON. Either run az bicep build yourself first (above), or delete the old JSON and let the script rebuild it:
Remove-Item main.json, custom-domain.json -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
2 — validate before a real deploy
az deployment group validate -g rg-tusharpuri -f main.bicep -p namePrefix=segue14 ...
az deployment group what-if  -g rg-tusharpuri -f main.bicep -p namePrefix=segue14 ...
! what-if reads the live resource directly and won't catch every class of bug — this repo's own circular-dependency error in custom-domain.bicep only ever surfaced on a real deploy. Treat what-if as a fast first pass, not a substitute for testing the real thing.
3 — republish
.\publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1 -StorageAccount fhirbridgedeploy -ResourceGroup rg-tusharpuri

Prints the fresh, cache-busted Portal URLs for both steps — use those, not any link you had open in a browser tab from before the edit.

i Editing a createUiDefinition*.json file instead? There's nothing to compile — just save it and go straight to step 3 (republish).

Push a new version

All 5 images share one tag — main.bicep reads ${imageRegistryServer}/<name>:${imageTag} for every one of them, so a release is really "get these 5 repositories to the same new tag," not 5 separate processes.

ImageSourceHow it's produced
fhirbridge-appcontainerization/docker/fhirbridge-app/DockerfileBuilt locally from this repo's source
demo-appcontainerization/docker/demo-app/DockerfileBuilt locally from this repo's source
fhirbridge-workercontainerization/docker/worker/DockerfileBuilt locally from this repo's source
fhirbridge-rediscontainerization/docker/redis-tls/DockerfileBuilt locally — stock redis:7-alpine plus the committed self-signed TLS cert
hapi-terminologydocker.io/hapiproject/hapi:latest (third-party, not ours)Not built — server-to-server copied straight into ACR via az acr import, no local Docker involved

1 — Log in to the registry

Azure CLI
az acr login --name seguebuilds

2 — Build, push, and import all 5 under the new tag

PowerShell
cd containerization/scripts
.\build-images.ps1 -Registry seguebuilds.azurecr.io -Tag v1.2.2 -Push
Bash
cd containerization/scripts
./build-images.sh -r seguebuilds.azurecr.io -t v1.2.2 -p

One command does everything: docker build + docker push for the 4 local images, then az acr import to copy hapi-terminology in from Docker Hub under the same tag. fhirbridge-app and demo-app get --build-arg APP_VERSION=<tag> automatically (shown in their footer) — fhirbridge-worker/fhirbridge-redis have no UI, so they don't take it.

! Requires Docker running locally, and pushing needs a registry you're already logged into (step 1). Add -HapiTerminologySource <image> (PowerShell) or -s <image> (Bash) to pin a specific upstream hapi-terminology release instead of whatever Docker Hub's :latest happens to be that day.

3 — Verify all 5 landed on the new tag

Azure CLI
for repo in fhirbridge-app fhirbridge-worker demo-app fhirbridge-redis hapi-terminology; do
  az acr repository show-tags --name seguebuilds --repository "$repo" --orderby time_desc -o tsv
done

4 — Point the wizard at it

Update createUiDefinition.json's Version tab default (imageTag) to the new tag, then republish (phase 02) so new one-click deploys pick it up automatically. Anyone deploying via the CLI just passes imageTag=<new-tag> directly and doesn't need this step.

containerization/azure-deploy/createUiDefinition.json
"name": "imageTag",
"defaultValue": "v1.2.2",
✕ All 5 images share one tag, but main.bicep has no per-image fallback — if even one repository is missing the new tag, that one container app fails to pull and the whole Step 1 deploy fails partway through. Always verify step 3 shows the new tag for all 5 repos before bumping the wizard default or handing the tag out to anyone.
i Shortcut for a release that only touches some of the 5 images (e.g. a C#-only fix in fhirbridge-app/fhirbridge-worker): instead of rebuilding images whose source didn't change, retag their existing content straight in the registry — a same-registry az acr import is a server-to-server copy, no Docker needed, and produces a byte-identical image under the new tag:
Azure CLI
az acr import --name seguebuilds --registry seguebuilds \
  --source demo-app:v1.2.1 --image demo-app:v1.2.2 --force
Only safe when you're certain that image's Dockerfile/source is unchanged for this release — otherwise rebuild it properly with step 2 above.

Real incident: this exact failure, live

Captured while writing this runbook — the wizard's Version default was bumped to v1.2.1 before that tag existed for all 5 images. Kept here as a concrete worked example of the danger callout above.

Checking the registry confirmed it: demo-app, fhirbridge-redis, and hapi-terminology topped out at v1.2.0, while fhirbridge-app already had v1.2.1 (from an earlier, narrower release):

Fixed with the same-registry retag shortcut above (no Docker rebuild needed, since none of these 3 images' source had actually changed) — all 3 landed on v1.2.1 within the same minute:

Troubleshooting

SymptomRoot causeFix
UNAUTHORIZED pulling hapi-terminology:v1.2.0 Container app config was missing ACR registries/secrets entirely fixed already applied in main.bicep
hapi-terminology-postgres crash-loop Postgres initdb needs chmod 700; Azure Files (SMB) can't do Unix chmod at all fixed volume switched to EmptyDir
Deploy error: circular dependency detected custom-domain.bicep read + wrote the same container app in one template fixed write routed through custom-domain-app-update.bicep module
RequireCustomHostnameInEnvironment Certificate created/bound before the hostname existed on the app Use custom-domain.bicep as-is — it always registers the hostname first and waits for it to finish
InvalidCustomHostNameValidation DNS (CNAME/TXT) hasn't propagated yet Wait for DNS to resolve (phase 05), then re-run Step 2 — always safe
502 Bad Gateway / crash-loop on /api/v1/config CryptographicException — a DataProtection key was never persisted to the shared key-ring (first-boot race) fixed DbSecretStore now catches it and lets the existing self-heal logic regenerate the secret
Deploy-to-Azure wizard field silently blank createUiDefinition quirks — resourceGroup().id doesn't exist; bracket indexing is invalid; only one property-chain level is honored after steps(...) fixed explicit ID concat + first()/last() + string-search extraction

Do / do not

Do

  • Confirm DNS has actually propagated before running Step 2
  • Re-run Step 2 freely — it's idempotent, even for already-bound domains
  • Use the automation scripts if you don't want to babysit DNS propagation
  • Re-run publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1 after any template edit

Do not

  • Deploy Step 2 before DNS has propagated — it fails cleanly, but there's no way to skip the wait
  • Test outside the agreed Ragu / Sponsorship subscription
  • Leave a bound custom domain out of template params on a later apply (IaC drift risk)

Local development reference

Not part of the Azure deploy flow, but the other set of commands and URLs you'll reach for day to day.

Backend (.NET 9)
dotnet build
dotnet test
dotnet run --project src/Api/FHIRBridge.Api        # http://localhost:5000, Swagger at /swagger
dotnet run --project src/Worker/FHIRBridge.Worker
Frontend (Angular 20)
cd portal
npm install
npm start      # http://localhost:4200
npm run build
npm test
Local E2E stack
docker-compose up -d
# Seq (structured logs):  http://localhost:5341
# Adminer (database UI):  http://localhost:8080
